cards.text: Jerusalem is large and spacious, friend, but there are few people in it, and the houses haven't been rebuilt yet (Nehemiah 7:4). A big city with hardly anybody home? That's a cookie box with three cookies rattling around in it, so now it's time to settle people in the holy city.

cards.question: Filling up the holy city starts at the top. Which group settles in Jerusalem first?
The rest of the people cast lots to choose who else moves in. The lots pick ___ out of every ten people to live in Jerusalem.
After the lots are cast, the other nine out of every ten stay in their own towns.
Some men step up on their own and volunteer to live in Jerusalem. How do the people treat the men who volunteer?

cards.text: Then comes the roll call of who settles in Jerusalem: families from Judah and Benjamin, priests, Levites, and gatekeepers who keep watch at the gates. Every group gets a head count, right down to the number. I tried counting the dust in my old junk drawer once, friend. I gave up at SEVEN.

Everyone else spreads out over the villages of Judah and Benjamin. Judah's people settle all the way from Beersheba to the Valley of Hinnom, and Benjamin's settle in towns like Michmash and Bethel. I spent YEARS in one drawer, and these folks get a whole map!

Next, the record goes back to the priests and Levites who went up with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua the high priest, two of the men the exiles came home with (Ezra 2:1-2; Haggai 1:1). It traces the priestly families down the generations, plus Levites giving praise and thanksgiving as David the man of God prescribed, and gatekeepers guarding the storerooms, all the way to the days of Nehemiah the governor and Ezra the priest and scribe. Generations of names, friend, and every one of them written DOWN. Trust me, I know what that's worth. And this city's story? NOT done.
